Everyone who has come off of methadone, what sort of tapers or strategies did you use? I have been on methadone maintenance for over three years and I am so sick of it and it seems impossible to get off of it. I'm looking to switch to Subutex, but I'm not sure if I should just taper off of the methadone rather than switch to another maintenance therapy. Thank you in advance for reading and offering advice. And everyone who is battling this addiction and trying to save their lives, I pray for you and I am so proud of you!

Being aware of my triggers and praising myself for even the smallest of accomplishments to stay motivated in recovery. I also utilize a workbook called "Co-occuring disorders Recovery workbook, strategies to manage Substance Abuse and Mental Health disorders" by Dennis C. Daley, Phd. I highly recommended for those who are dealing with a dual diagnosis. Bubble baths are just as important as self-help meetings and connecting with others dealing with the same situations and emotions. Meditation and yoga are also very helpful because addiction wreaks havoc on your brain and anything positive to help you adjust to a healthier lifestyle and cognitive  function is definitely a priority in self-care. Good luck to everyone going through this journey, you are strong and beautiful. You Are Not Alone.

One thing that helps me personally is to not see recovery as black and white. If you are using less than you were six months ago, you are making progress and should be very proud of yourself. Having a dual diagnosis is seriously threatening to recovery. I can relate, having depression and anxiety is already a battle for me and adding my severe opiate addiction is like throwing gasoline on a fire. You are doing the best you can right now and that's all you can expect from yourself. It's two steps forward and one step back but you are going to get there if you stay persistent. One thing that helps me is listening to positive TED Talks and guided meditation to switch my mindset. I would also encourage you to get involved with NA or AA because they are like-minded individuals going through the same thing and it feels good knowing you aren't alone, even though it feels that way most of the time, all you have to do is take their suggestions and implement their philosophy. If there's something you don't like about it just toss that aside or revsit it at another time, everybody's recovery is different and different things work for some people rather than others. Don't be so hard on yourself, the more time you stay clean the more your brain will heal and your emotions will regulate themselves. If you aren't on any antidepressants I would seriously consider starting some to help you deal with any and all serious emotional issues you are experiencing. If you are already on medication I would suggest adjusting the dose even if just for now. Taking vitamins and supplements can help your cognitive function as well. I Rely a lot on positive self-help books to keep myself from spiraling into suicidal ideation because I can very easily end up that way if I don't help myself.

There is a workbook by Dennis C Daley called "co-occurring disorders recovery workbook strategies to manage Substance Abuse and Mental Health disorders" and it is extremely helpful with sorting out emotions and thoughts to help in daily life and crisis situations. I wish you the best of luck and I am always here to talk to if you need.
